question: If a right circular cone of height 24 cm has a volume of 1232 cm³, then the total surface area of the cone is:
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Volume = (1/3)πr²h = 1232 ⇒ (1/3) × (22/7) × r² × 24 = 1232

⇒ r² = (1232 × 7) ÷ 176 = 49 ⇒ r = 7 cm.

Using the standard Pythagorean triplet (7, 24, 25), the slant height l = 25 cm.

TSA = πr(r + l) = (22/7) × 7 × (7 + 25) = 22 × 32 = 704 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 704 cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/43c48651618071dd31ade0d537da8ffb5b74d8d58adb875f23f19dbc527d520b.png] 

**Given:**

Height of the cone (h) = 24 cm

Volume of the cone (V) = 1232 cm³

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cone = (1/3)πr²h

Slant height (l) = √(r² + h²)

Total Surface Area (TSA) = πr(r + l)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 1232 = (1/3) × (22/7) × r² × 24

⇒ 1232 = (176/7) × r²

⇒ r² = (1232 × 7) ÷ 176

⇒ r² = 49

⇒ Radius (r) = 7 cm

⇒ Slant height (l) = √(7² + 24²)

⇒ l = √(49 + 576)

⇒ l = √625 = 25 cm

⇒ TSA = (22/7) × 7 × (7 + 25)

⇒ TSA = 22 × 32 = 704 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 704 cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area of a Cone

The curved surface area (CSA) covers only the lateral curved side of the cone. Formula: CSA = πrl.

Volume of a Cone

The internal capacity of a cone is exactly one-third of the volume of a cylinder with the same base and height. Formula: V = (1/3)πr²h.

Pythagorean Triplets

Standard sets of integers that satisfy a² + b² = c² speed up geometry computations considerably. Common examples: (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (7, 24, 25), and (8, 15, 17).
